WoW: Forever

Feral — Bear Druid

Leather tanking in Bear Form on rage and dodge: no block, no parry. This is your only combat form between levels 10 and 20, so every Druid plays it whether they intend to tank or not.

WoW: Forever · Tank · Updated October 8, 2026 · Beta build 1.60.1.70245 · Null Ossuary

Levelling guide, 1 to 60. The beta is capped at level 30 as of the October 1 build, raised from 20 that day, so no level-60 Bear build has been tested. Bear and Cat share one talent tree and mostly one build. They have separate pages here because the rotations, stat priorities and gear are completely different even where the talents are not. No source has posted a level 30 build either: the cap only reached 30 on October 1, and none of the three has published one since. The level 30 line below extends the published level 20 build using the full talent tree's point costs, not a build any guide has recommended. Blizzard's own caveat: "class abilities and talents may continue to evolve throughout the beta test and are subject to additional changes."

What Bear is for

Bear Form multiplies the armour on your gear and adds +180 health, and you can drop form to heal yourself with Mana. GrowlGrowlLevel 10 · Spell · Physical · Rank 1 of 7CastInstantRangeMeleeCooldown8 sec cooldownDuration3 secTaunts the target to attack you, but has no effect if the target is already attacking you. on an 8-second cooldown holds what you pull, and rage comes from being hit as well as from hitting. In Forever the weapon's damage counts in Bear Form, so more damage means more threat.

You do not get a choice before level 20. Bear Form comes from a class quest at 10; Cat Form does not exist until 20. The published advice: "As you reach Level 10 you will mainly want to level in Bear Form, using your Mana to heal yourself after killing enemies, and then recovering your Mana while in Bear Form."

The class starts slowly: "Since Bear Form is not unlocked until Level 10, and Cat Form first at level 20, Feral Druid has a fairly slow start."

The three-tank line-up of Protection Warrior, Protection Paladin and Feral Druid is a common assumption rather than a Blizzard taxonomy. Blizzard's own Druid deep dive credits Druids with the "ability to serve any combat role" and publishes no tank list.

Stat priority

Stamina and armour first, then Agility (dodge and more armour), then Defense.

Bear Form multiplies your gear's armour, so a leather piece with a high armour number beats the same stats on cloth. The weapon's damage now counts in Bear Form, and more damage means more threat, so choose the weapon on its stats and its damage together. Blizzard describes the mechanism: auto-attack DPS in Bear, Cat or Dire Bear Form equals your weapon's DPS outright. The swing speed is a fixed 2.5 seconds in Bear and Dire Bear, 1.0 second in Cat Form, and weapon-damage abilities use the same numbers. Blizzard publishes the two speeds but not which form takes which, so that pairing is ours, not a source's.

One published tank list orders it Defense > Dodge > Armor > Agility > Strength > Attack Power > crit > Haste. One source disputes the weapon-damage priority outright, arguing you should "Compare the item's form-relevant bonuses, armor, Stamina and defense instead of importing a Warrior list." Three sources and the client data are on the other side, but the disagreement is real.

This amount can be further increased by multipliers from those forms. is a different talent under the same name (above): base armour per level and defense scaling, rather than a percentage of your gear.

The druid is considered in combat for the duration. front-loads: "Instantly generates 10 Rage and another 20 Rage over 10 sec", where Classic gave 20 over 10 with nothing up front.
  • Bear Form and Dire Bear Form now generate 75% increased Rage on a critical strike (October 1), which is another reason crit gear is not wasted on a tank.
  • All Shapeshift Forms are now immune to Disarm (October 1). The nuance matters for a tank: if you are disarmed before you shift, the form does not clear the Disarm, and you deal reduced damage for its duration. A mob or boss that disarms you before you can shift still works.
  • Bear Form's health bonus went from +20 to +180.
